brief.title: Election update: Monday, November 9 (morning)
brief.markdown:
# Election update: Monday, November 9 (morning)

## Bottom line
The House results table now marks 420 of 435 races called: D 257, R 163, with 218 needed for a majority ([House table](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_United_States_House_of_Representatives_elections)). Counting FL-07, which two outlets report Ryan Elijah (R) won, it is D 257, R 164. In the Senate, Democrats have secured 54 seats to Republicans' 44, counting seats not up, with 51 needed ([Senate table](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_United_States_Senate_elections)). Alaska and Mississippi are still uncalled, and USA Today reports legal fights loom in both ([USA Today](https://news.google.?oc=5)). No seat rated safe is within 5 points. With 90.5% of competitive races called, the tracker's forecaster scorecard is ready (Lessons learned, below).

## Called since the last update
- **MN-01 (Jake Johnson, D gain):** marked called in the Wikipedia results table, following AP ([House table](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_United_States_House_of_Representatives_elections)). Brad Finstad (R) has requested a recount, the New Ulm Journal reports ([New Ulm Journal](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMihAFBVV95cUxQRG4zTUdmSnBRQkN0UTBUd1U1Y1MxOFhKYmdERXRDeURNb1V4azF5ZFQ3OHJVSHFHWGpJc0U0bVRuNUpDMXF2dTlDYUVNZG5kWFBYdDlPRWROQzZvSno1bHlxYnpuZWIzd3BYQ1RQVkhiWTAxaU5SdWlQU3FBdk9FWlMyOHk?oc=5)).
- **NC-07 (David Rouzer, R hold):** marked called in the table ([House table](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_United_States_House_of_Representatives_elections)).
- **Reported, not yet in the table:** the Orlando Sentinel reports Ryan Elijah (R) won FL-07 ([Orlando Sentinel](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMitwFBVV95cUxNWnRpN18tZWFNNWhabk1iT0FvM0paYW4wajRZZ19HZGJUczNWOVFwTUVlYk1ZbDY0OXpXSVVzUjN1WmRWZmtfOVBFNkZBSGRwN2Y3ZnFIdUprRjJWS29hUFZraXhVWmpURXBNQW1aUnFYamt6RHdDVzdONnd5c0RleEdyOTRObjhMRjdTWkpnY2dUWkNwM2tZM1YzV3p0Zm9ZbE5Ub0RVWXpkay1FZWg2R25UUm1XRnM?oc=5)), and the Daytona Beach News-Journal reports he claimed the win ([News-Journal](https://news.google.?oc=5)). Counted separately until the table follows.

## Still uncalled
One line for every competitive race the table hasn't marked called, Senate first.
- **AK Senate** (Tossup): Gov. Mike Dunleavy gave a vote-count update describing a "very close" race, The Hill reports ([The Hill](https://news.google.?oc=5)).
- **MS Senate** (Likely R): Mississippi Today reports DeSoto County, a Republican stronghold, was key to Scott Colom's (D) performance ([Mississippi Today](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiiwFBVV95cUxPWUltQXhZblVjSmZPcHlodDN3UUhZZzcxa25KZjhVY0FFUXFXZDJyZ3VtLUllbVJXV3FNRC1Wa1JiVWZFRWtMaVlaaXBjcHVseS01LW5xdVI5akk3OXIwaDBVc0Q1OExULVMtODlWaFRRcU9fa2JtTEhXaUFrRnRRSG1GRVJTQkFMdEFF?oc=5)); MS NOW reported Saturday that Colom's lead had widened ([MS NOW](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMif0FVX3lxTE9iNUpNaEtQUVI0RDBjdkdSQndjZmI4V0doZ3ZrbUNtb0E2RVNiNDdVSHVmblgzUE5VeFcwSWY1SXZLeW9rbmpvT3g4MkNjb3U3ZVlHRmpCNHV5aGozN2NwMTFhcGhxeVcxMVpMM2ttZzF0SERvT2VSMzdYcVY4TTA?oc=5)).
- **AK-AL** (Lean R): still on CBS News's list of races without a winner ([CBS](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMijAFBVV95cUxPTm1vVUVNdk1FNWRfMFlpenMya2pETU00SkhBNGFQOTJGSTlKTDYyTmRLZElSd0ZfOU9oTW83aE5IZnN3SjZPVmZpQ2NuVUZGWTE1bzFMVHpmMDhNQU5uOGV4MGlERlRoeWJ0bG5RcmtaOG1GLUdQS05nN3pVanBtS1BaMHhCc21mS0gtcA?oc=5)).
- **AZ-02** (Lean R): today's news query failed (HTTP 503); the last report had Eli Crane (R) ahead of Jonathan Nez (D) ([results table](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_United_States_House_of_Representatives_elections)).
- **CO-04** (Lean R): trailing Eileen Laubacher (D), Lauren Boebert's (R) campaign alleges "unusual voting patterns," the Denver Gazette reports; that is a campaign's claim ([Denver Gazette](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMirgFBVV95cUxObkVRU09BbWQ4WG5nTEpmcWg2bXRTRWR2c29vM0xQbE9VRGNVQTRMS2VHNGd4YlRUanNWQVY3OUtiaVJRNnI1ZEN4Q3BiQWF0MkMxMVB3Yy1PclZIbnZvM2h2Tm00cjhPQzBaUWhYSjh1MFhHa01yYzVNcWhOOUw2b1c4WUlzM2tFazNGZzlocnlKeVJoM3FNbFN0cWxTMEtvQWlMTFdLbG5sUTZ0a1E?oc=5)). The campaign expects a recount ([KDVR](https://news.google.?oc=5)).
- **FL-07** (Lean R): reported won by Ryan Elijah (R), per the [Orlando Sentinel](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMitwFBVV95cUxNWnRpN18tZWFNNWhabk1iT0FvM0paYW4wajRZZ19HZGJUczNWOVFwTUVlYk1ZbDY0OXpXSVVzUjN1WmRWZmtfOVBFNkZBSGRwN2Y3ZnFIdUprRjJWS29hUFZraXhVWmpURXBNQW1aUnFYamt6RHdDVzdONnd5c0RleEdyOTRObjhMRjdTWkpnY2dUWkNwM2tZM1YzV3p0Zm9ZbE5Ub0RVWXpkay1FZWg2R25UUm1XRnM?oc=5); not yet marked in the table.
- **FL-27** (Lean R): the recount is set for Monday, the Miami-Dade supervisor of elections says ([NBC 6](https://news.google.?oc=5)).
- **NC-03** (Likely R): today's news query failed; the last reported count had Greg Murphy (R) ahead by 233 votes ([results table](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_United_States_House_of_Representatives_elections)).
- **NC-05** (Likely R): Virginia Foxx (R) trailed Chuck Hubbard (D) by 99 votes in the last reported count, per [Carolina Public Press](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMipAFBVV95cUxQcGlsWk1nRFlFLWRDTTJyWDhPVXh1VFU2enRMN0VhOGNtdm1NNE9kZzU1Q2p6cVJzX3RFMW42UmdzZEFBZVVaelBTRFlITHVOcm9sV1AtenZvSS1zYVJJc1VlcGZmUlZmZHhBaTlXaDZTZXFtYmszcUNhZEdRUExNemJ4a3hCeWJCZnVaUldmVlRPLWxMdmpoR1hrZVRPOXUxbDdmYQ?oc=5).
- **WA-05** (Likely R): Michael Baumgartner (R) has claimed victory, but the race has not been officially called, per [KREM](https://news.google.?oc=5).
- **Safe seats:** 7 seats rated safe are not yet marked in the table. That is table lag, not close races ([full list](https://jakeworcester-byte.github.io/political-tracker/#results)).

## Recounts and certification
- **Florida:** the FL-27 recount is scheduled for Monday amid a pending lawsuit, CBS News reports ([CBS](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMimwFBVV95cUxOckJSZFJPbkpZUk9EbXhyNFZYcFdUazE5dUFQVEY0eHpoRkxHUHZZYnNYRU5KYkhaSzdkRjVwVFJIY0w3V1ZxbnNPdnFFSkRsU0c1cVhnd3Z4eXl1VGdvMXNTOUo4WWpsM3h3MWRPZ0l3ODRGZERGUGhGbHJTYTBOek0zeGJIbnVZVWFsLVpyWnBVZm9zaUF1VWgxUQ?oc=5)).
- **Minnesota:** Finstad has requested a recount in MN-01 even after the table marked the race for Johnson ([New Ulm Journal](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMihAFBVV95cUxQRG4zTUdmSnBRQkN0UTBUd1U1Y1MxOFhKYmdERXRDeURNb1V4azF5ZFQ3OHJVSHFHWGpJc0U0bVRuNUpDMXF2dTlDYUVNZG5kWFBYdDlPRWROQzZvSno1bHlxYnpuZWIzd3BYQ1RQVkhiWTAxaU5SdWlQU3FBdk9FWlMyOHk?oc=5)).
- **Colorado:** the Boebert campaign expects a recount in CO-04 ([KDVR](https://news.google.?oc=5)).

## Legal and federal action
- **Florida:** in Rodriguez v. Garcia (S.D. Fla.), the federal case over the FL-27 recount, a response opposing a motion was filed Nov. 8 with two exhibits ([CourtListener](https://www.courtlistener.com/docket/75084109/rodriguez-v-garcia-et-al/)).
- **Alaska:** Mary Peltola's (D) campaign sued for records on rejected absentee ballots, Reuters reports ([Reuters](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiuwFBVV95cUxNb2Y0QkZDU3lpQXJjc2ZuYWlvT3lMM0wyTDFqZkI5Q3VWS1dycnhHaElwLU9NeVJ2Y1MzaVVCb1EzZlU4U2RadjVYZHo1cGV1eFZYYWsySW9vZ3ZnbWxYc2JXODhsVHlrYko1VmZEV29WY1hoYXJyUVNZbnhXOTdIZGU1U0xqb3gxS2VwWDh4Rnk2NVFUMHlmU0Fqa3RpZk5lclhld1JRdmRZcWJlbmVIR29IX0w4YjRqaV9V?oc=5)).
- **Washington state:** a judge ruled federal officials cannot force Washington to set aside alleged noncitizen ballots, The Seattle Times reports ([Seattle Times](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMivwFBVV95cUxNTzY1YjlrXzBmdi1iWDFQUFZ2Um5GN1I2OWswVnl2aFlHNXV3QXVndWJuYzFMWHo5dG04RGFILUVfVi1ERGZUQWl6R3pyRXAyNXhzMjlFcDVBVk5nT0ZEOVJONlVqenVIZjZ1bkhTRlA2TjNoSVdwaEZDX2tmNWlZQkdSNk9USTc4ZnRJV1ljQ3BYMXVLdkdyX0tmT3ZLeFNoNFplLUdxWXVmc2VuZVA1UFVRemZMUm1kRmRUM0tVYw?oc=5)).

## Lessons learned
From the tracker's scorecard, which compares each forecaster's final pre-election rating with races marked called ([scorecard](https://jakeworcester-byte.github.io/political-tracker/#results)):
- **Forecasters:** the consensus rating was right in 133 races and wrong in 18, and every miss went toward Democrats, among them NV-02, FL-09, MN-01 and NC-06, a seat rated Solid R. Of the 16 races the consensus called a Tossup, Democrats won 15.
- **Who did best:** RealClearPolling had the highest hit rate on non-tossup calls (94.2%), but it left 29 races as Tossups; among outlets that rated nearly every race, Silver Bulletin (90.6%) and Split Ticket (91.0%) led. The Economist (86.1%) and Inside Elections (86.8%) trailed.
- **Markets:** Polymarket's final prices gave Democrats 94.5% for the House and 76.5% for the Senate; Democrats won both.
- **Polls:** too few called races have vote shares in the table to judge yet (one so far).

## Coverage note
- **Parser:** the results tables parsed (435 House, 35 Senate) and the parser check is healthy.
- **News errors:** 2 of 17 race news queries failed (HTTP 503 from Google News), so AZ-02 and NC-03 have no fresh lead.
- **Court records:** CourtListener used (3 requests; 24 election dockets and 1 opinion).
- **Scorecard:** ready; vote shares are still sparse, so the poll check will fill in over the coming days.
